rationale: The obligation asks whether the supersession statement establishes that enforceable effluent limits and monitoring requirements are exclusively those in Parts I–IV of the current issuance, rather than any unrestate terms of the September 30, 2016 issuance. The packet grounds that the current permit uses the same number (NM0020583), is effective December 1, 2021 through November 30, 2026, states that it supersedes and replaces the 2016 issuance, and authorizes discharge in accordance with conditions set forth in Parts I–IV. That supports that current Parts I–IV conditions apply, but it does not establish exclusivity: the packet does not include the text of Parts I–IV, the 2016 permit, or any passage showing that unrestate 2016 terms cannot remain enforceable. ACCEPT would require grounded evidence that exclusivity follows from supersession plus the cited authorization language; REJECT would require grounded evidence that the statement fails to establish exclusivity. Neither burden is met, and absence of the missing terms is not closed-world evidence of distinct enforceability outcomes. Per P5, unsupported uncertainty is preferred to unsupported semantic closure.
